commits.message:
feat(taxonomy): recruiter-facing skill descriptions, GlossaryTech-style

Adds a description field to canonical skills: one plain-language
sentence explaining what the skill is and what it's used for, written
for a non-technical IT recruiter reading a resume -- the same job
GlossaryTech does, scoped to what Hermes already has (skills seen in
real postings) rather than a public crowdsourced dictionary, which
isn't the right fit for a single-tenant internal tool with no public
user base.

app/understanding/taxonomy/descriptions.py: generate_skill_description()
calls the LiteLLM gateway directly (_call_litellm_with_model, same
function every other Hermes AI capability eventually routes through --
no direct provider calls) with a short instruction to write one
25-word-max, jargon-free sentence. Not routed through a registered
Langfuse prompt like the live parsing pipeline's LLM fallback -- this
only ever runs from an admin action (approving a candidate, or the
one-time backfill script below), never in the request path of a real
email being parsed, so the tracing a registered prompt buys isn't
needed the same way here. Strictly best-effort: litellm_configured()
guard, broad exception catch, returns None on any failure -- a missing
description must never break an approval or a script run.

app/understanding/taxonomy/loader.py: add_canonical_skill takes an
optional description; new set_skill_description() fills or overwrites
one on an existing entry, same transaction-scoped advisory lock as the
rest of this file's writes.

approve_taxonomy_candidate (app/understanding/taxonomy/candidates.py):
when approving a skill candidate, generates a description automatically
unless one's already known -- every newly-approved skill gets defined
without extra admin effort, wrapped in its own try/except so a
generation failure still lets the approval itself succeed.

scripts/hermes-taxonomy-generate-descriptions.py: one-time backfill for
the skills that predate this feature. Only fills missing descriptions,
never overwrites; safe to re-run if it's interrupted partway through,
since each skill is written and cache-busted individually.

Frontend: SkillsTaxonomyPage now shows each skill's description
directly under its name (the aliases move into a hover tooltip on the
name instead of their own column) -- description is also now part of
the search match, so "container orchestration" finds Kubernetes even
if the word "Kubernetes" itself isn't typed.

New coverage: description generation returns None cleanly with no
LiteLLM key configured (the actual CI/test environment) rather than
raising; set_skill_description persists on a real entry and reports
failure (not an exception) for an unknown one; approving a skill
candidate succeeds even when no description could be generated. Full
regression suite (18 checks) green. Frontend type-checks and builds
clean.
